tests.description: Timed check on Natural and Manufactured Timber

questions.question: Explain why plywood is less likely to warp than solid timber of the same thickness.
questions.correctAnswer: Solid timber has grain in one direction - it warps along the grain as moisture changes. Plywood's alternating veneer layers create opposing grain directions that cancel out warping forces.

questions.question: A designer is making a kitchen worktop. Compare solid oak and MDF, justifying your recommendation.
questions.correctAnswer: Solid oak: beautiful grain, very durable, water-resistant with treatment - but expensive, can warp, heavy. MDF: smooth, uniform, does not warp, affordable - but swells if water penetrates, cannot be refinished.

questions.question: Discuss the environmental advantages and disadvantages of using hardwoods in product design.
questions.correctAnswer: Advantages: durable (products last decades), repairable, biodegradable, carbon-neutral if sustainably sourced. Disadvantages: slow growth, deforestation risk, high transport miles, illegal logging concerns. FSC certification helps.

questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: identify ash properties (excellent steam-bending, attractive grain, strong and flexible); identify plywood properties (can be laminated into curves, dimensionally stable); conclude: ash for premium one-off chairs, plywood for mass production.
